thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated generation latency detected in eu-west-1 for hosted text/generation endpoints. Error rate low but p95 generation latency > 6s. Paging oncall now.

alice jensen: Oncall here, looking. Can someone grab perf dashboard? I'll start investigating routing and model fallback. /whoami -> alice (oncall).

ben choi: pulling logs. seeing steady CPU saturation on pool-gpu-eu-3 around 09:12 UTC. memory looks fine.

carla mendez: I can start drafting the status page copy. Do we know customer impact?

alice jensen: Early read -> most requests succeed but slow. Some customers with tight latency SLOs will see errors/timeouts if they have 3s client timeouts. Broad impact: degraded latency for eu-west-1 gen endpoints. No data exfiltration.

dave_h: tagging infra: looks like a kernel driver patch rollout caused reduced GPU throughput on a subset of nodes. NDP shows 10 nodes in degraded perf. Rolling back the kernel update on affected hosts now.

carla mendez: Draft statuspage initial: ```We are investigating elevated generation latency impacting the eu-west-1 region. Users may experience slower response times for text generation and streaming. Our on-call team is investigating the root cause and applying mitigations. No data loss or security impact identified. Next update in ~30 minutes or sooner if there are significant developments.```

emily-pm: :eyes: Good. Add note about potential fallbacks and recommended temporary mitigations for customers (re-route to other regions or use smaller model).

carla mendez: Updated draft: ```We are investigating elevated generation latency impacting the eu-west-1 region. Some customers may experience slower response times or timeouts for text generation. Our team is applying a mitigative rollback to a recent kernel update and routing fallback to adjacent regions where capacity is available. No data loss or security impact identified. Next update in 30 minutes or sooner if there are significant developments.```

alice jensen: +1. Ben, can you confirm if routing fallback is already in effect or needs a manual trigger?

ben choi: Automated routing policy should have started falling back to eu-central when latency crossed the threshold, but policy logs show only partial evictions. I'm manually triggering emergency fallback for high-priority tenant routes now.

incident-bot: ACTION: Pager handoff requested from alice jensen to ben choi at 09:28 UTC.

alice jensen: Handing off to @ben choi for investigation. Ben, feel free to escalate to infra if rollback doesn't finish in 10m.

ben choi: Acked. I'll keep the thread running and update status page when we have rollback progress or a measurable latency improvement.

carla mendez: I'll prepare the second update with timing: approx 15–20m after rollback starts. Also preparing customer-facing blurb for high-volume tenants.

ops-runbook-bot: RUNBOOK STEP: rollback_kernel_update -> initiated by dave_h at 09:30 UTC. Expected step duration: 10-12 minutes. Monitor GPU scheduler and p95 tokens/sec.

ben choi: Rollback completed on 6/10 degraded nodes at 09:40 UTC. p95 latency trending down from ~7.2s to ~3.5s on those hosts. Still seeing elevated p95 overall due to remaining nodes.

carla mendez: Statuspage update #2 draft: ```Update (09:45 UTC): We have identified a recent kernel update deployment as the likely cause of reduced GPU throughput on a subset of hosts in eu-west-1. Our engineers have rolled back the update on the affected hosts; partial recovery is visible. We continue to apply rollbacks and are also enabling routing fallback to adjacent regions for affected traffic. We expect further improvements in the next 15 minutes.```

emily-pm: Add estimated ETA to resolution? Maybe 'within 60 minutes' if optimistic.

carla mendez: Added ETA: ```We expect full recovery within 60 minutes but will update earlier if resolved.```

alice jensen: Quick note for internal comms: tell support to inform customers with short timeouts to extend to 10s or use retry/backoff for now.

carla mendez: Customer message variant for high-volume tenants: ```We are seeing elevated latency in eu-west-1 for text generation. We are rolling back a kernel update and redirecting workloads to adjacent regions; please consider routing to eu-central temporarily or increasing client timeouts to avoid spurious failures. Contact support if you need assistance.```

ben choi: All rollback tasks finished at 09:55 UTC. p95 across eu-west-1 now ~1.4s (normal baseline ~1.2s). No errors introduced by rollback.

incident-bot: METRIC: p95_latency_eu_west_1 : 1.45s (09:56 UTC)

carla mendez: Preparing resolved notice. Draft resolved: ```Resolved (10:00 UTC): The elevated generation latency in eu-west-1 has been resolved. A recent kernel update caused reduced GPU throughput on a subset of hosts; our engineers rolled back the update and enabled routing fallbacks. Systems have recovered to baseline performance. If you continue to experience issues, please contact support and provide request IDs and timestamps. We apologize for the disruption.```

emily-pm: Good. Add note about follow-up postmortem and potential customer credits investigation.

carla mendez: Added: 'A follow-up post-incident report will be published within 72 hours.'

dave_h: Posting ops note: hosts with the kernel update will be quarantined until a validated patch is available; rolling updates paused.

alice jensen: Publishing status page now. Support informed via #support-notify with the customer message template.

incident-bot: STATUSPAGE: Initial -> Published at 09:14 UTC; Update -> Published at 09:46 UTC; Resolved -> Published at 10:00 UTC

ben choi: I'll leave monitoring alerts on and will be available for 2 hours for any regression.

carla mendez: Thanks team. I'll draft the postmortem skeleton and ping the incident review channel. :thumbsup:

emily-pm: Great job everyone. Closing thread after some cooldown.

ops-runbook-bot: REMINDER: create postmortem doc and include customer impact table, timeline, remediation, and action items.
